item.title: Draining peatlands leaves a long legacy of warming
item.description: Peatland ecosystems like bogs and swamps perform an important balancing act: Their vegetation takes up huge amounts of carbon dioxide, while their soil microbes produce methane. Although methane is a potent greenhouse gas, peatlands exhibit a net cooling effect on the planet because of the sheer scale of carbon dioxide they remove from the atmosphere, which has amounted to hundreds of gigatons globally over thousands of years. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Stabilizing atomically thin metals with sandwich structures: Machine learning expands the search
item.description: Atomically thin metals, metallenes, are promising materials for catalysis, electronics and energy conversion, but their synthesis has been challenging. Researchers from the University of Jyväskylä have now identified more than 300 stable metallene sandwich structures using machine learning and high-performance computing. The results provide researchers with a practical roadmap for the fabrication of new two-dimensional metals. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Certain fungi turn specialized plant cells into water-carrying cells using one protein
item.description: Can a pathogen that causes damage to a plant also make that plant more resilient to drought? An international research team led by the University of Göttingen has investigated this apparent paradox. The researchers discovered how certain fungi promote the formation of new water-conducting cells in plants. At the same time, infected plants showed increased tolerance to drought stress. The results were published in the journal Cell Host & Microbe. Fuente: Phys.org.
